raw_response:
I am old now, but I still farm the same land every year, and I do not like taking big risks. On my 30 mu, wheat and maize are the main way to keep income steady, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation. What I do is mostly based on what has worked on my fields and what the other farmers around here do. Fertilizer is expensive, water from the well also costs money, so I will not push too hard, but I also do not want the crop to go hungry. For wheat, I will sow in October like usual, use a common improved variety that is easy to buy locally, put most fertilizer at planting, then add some more at jointing if the stand looks weak. I will irrigate around the key stages, but not too many times unless the season turns dry. After wheat harvest, the maize must go in quickly. There is no time to fuss, so I will do simple field preparation and plant right away. Maize usually needs less watering here if the summer rains come, but I will still keep the well ready. I am careful with money because some family members work outside and cannot always help on time, so I rely mainly on family labor and only hire a little if harvest and planting crash together.
